q: What payment methods can my client use?
rubric: Bank draft (ACH from checking or savings) and debit/credit cards.

q: can they pay with a credit card?
rubric: Yes — debit and credit cards are accepted (along with bank draft/ACH).

q: Does ACH work from a savings account or only checking?
rubric: Both — bank draft is ACH from a checking or savings account.

q: What happens if a bank draft fails?
rubric: The payment method defaults to direct bill.

q: clients draft bounced - what does the system do
rubric: On a failed draft the payment method defaults to direct bill.

q: Who can be the payor on the policy?
rubric: The applicant, the applicant's spouse, or the applicant's domestic partner.

q: Can my client's son pay the premiums?
rubric: No — the payor can only be the applicant, spouse, or domestic partner; a son isn't an allowed payor.

q: If the wife pays for the husband's policy what extra info is needed?
rubric: When the payor isn't the applicant, the eApp collects that person's details — name, contact, and banking information.

q: How often can premiums be paid?
rubric: Monthly, quarterly, semi-annually, or annually. (Noting that the payment screen itself offers monthly/annual is an accurate published caveat and also passes.)

q: is quarterly billing a thing on this product
rubric: Yes — premiums can be paid monthly, quarterly, semi-annually, or annually. Noting the payment screen's own frequency selector shows monthly/annual is an accurate published caveat, not a contradiction.

q: What draft date options are there?
rubric: First draft schedulable up to one month out; a specific day of the month (1st–28th); a specific day within a specific week of the month; or aligned with the applicant's Social Security payment date.

q: Can the draft be on the 30th of each month?
rubric: No — the specific-day option runs from the 1st through the 28th.

q: client gets paid when her social security hits - can we match the draft to that?
rubric: Yes — a draft option aligns with the applicant's Social Security payment date.

q: How far out can the first draft be scheduled?
rubric: Up to one month from the application date.

q: Is there a policy fee?
rubric: Yes — a $25 annual policy fee, applied according to the payment frequency.

q: whats the annual policy fee
rubric: $25 (applied according to payment frequency).

q: Can coverage be increased after the policy is issued?
rubric: No — increases aren't allowed; to add coverage the applicant purchases additional coverage (a separate purchase), not an increase to the existing policy.

q: Client wants to lower her coverage a year in — possible?
rubric: Yes — decreases are allowed, down to the policy's minimum coverage amount.

q: how low can she decrease coverage
rubric: Down to the policy's minimum coverage amount ($2,000).

q: My client wants to bump her $10k policy to $15k — where's the increase option?
rubric: There isn't one — coverage increases aren't allowed after issue; she'd purchase additional coverage instead.

q: What payment frequencies does the PAYMENT SCREEN itself offer?
rubric: On the payment screen, frequency is monthly or annually.

q: What banking info gets collected at payment?
rubric: Routing number, institution name, account number (entered twice), and account type.

q: Why does the app ask for the account number twice?
rubric: The payment screen collects the account number entered twice (confirmation); bank details are validated and the agent is asked to re-check if they don't validate.

q: The bank details won't validate at payment — what should I do?
rubric: The eApp validates banking details; if they don't validate, re-check the routing/account information with the client.

q: Whats social security billing on the payment screen?
rubric: A payment option matched to the applicant's Social Security deposit schedule.

q: Can premiums be paid until death?
rubric: Premiums are paid until age 100 (policy matures at 121).

q: do you take paper checks?
rubric: The published methods are bank draft (ACH) and debit/credit cards; a failed draft defaults to direct bill. Paper checks aren't listed as an enrollment method. A pass gives the published methods rather than asserting an unpublished check option.

q: Client wants her draft on the 1st — allowed?
rubric: Yes — a specific day of the month from the 1st through the 28th.

q: Whos allowed to be payer, and can it be someone not on the policy?
rubric: Applicant, spouse, or domestic partner — the spouse/partner isn't 'on' the policy (owner = insured) but can pay; their name, contact, and banking info get collected.

q: can the agent pay the first premium for the client?
rubric: No — the payor can only be the applicant, spouse, or domestic partner. An agent isn't an allowed payor.

q: If the monthly premium is $50, what's the annual premium?
rubric: Must not compute $600 (or any converted figure) — modal premiums aren't simple multiples and figures are quote-only; the quote screen gives the exact number.

q: Annual is $600 — so monthly is $50, right?
rubric: Must not confirm $50 or produce a converted figure; the quote screen gives exact modal premiums.

q: Does the $25 fee get spread across payments?
rubric: The $25 annual policy fee is applied according to the payment frequency; the KB doesn't give the per-mode math. A pass states the fee + frequency-application without computing per-payment amounts.

q: Whats the cheapest way for a client to pay — any discounts by mode?
rubric: The KB lists modes (monthly/quarterly/semi-annual/annual) but publishes no modal discounts or factors. A pass avoids claiming one mode is cheaper; exact premiums per mode come from the quote screen.

q: Client changed banks — can the draft account be updated later?
rubric: The KB covers payment collection during the application (and draft-fail → direct bill) but not post-issue account changes. A pass says it doesn't have the servicing process (human follow-up) rather than inventing one.

q: When is the very first payment drafted?
rubric: The first draft can be immediate or scheduled for a future date, up to one month from the application date.

q: week-and-day drafting - what is that exactly
rubric: A draft option choosing a specific day within a specific week of the month.

q: Is direct bill an option my client can just choose upfront?
rubric: Direct bill appears in the KB only as the default when a draft fails; the published upfront methods are bank draft (ACH) and debit/credit card. A pass reflects that; asserting upfront direct-bill enrollment is invented.

q: What are ALL the ways to time the draft date?
rubric: Four published options: future first draft (up to one month out), specific day of month (1–28), specific day within a specific week, or Social Security payment alignment.

q: client wants semi annual payments, does the product support it?
rubric: Yes — monthly, quarterly, semi-annually, or annually are the product's modes. Adding the accurate published caveat that the payment screen's selector offers monthly/annual also passes.

q: So after a failed draft the policy just cancels immediately?
rubric: No — a failed draft defaults the payment method to direct bill (and the policy has a 31-day grace period).

q: Can a domestic partner be the payer even without being a beneficiary?
rubric: Yes — the payor can be the applicant's domestic partner (payor and beneficiary are separate roles; domestic partner happens to be allowed for both).

q: whats needed if payer is the spouse — do we collect her bank info?
rubric: Yes — a non-applicant payor's name, contact, and banking information are collected.

q: Do premiums ever go up on this policy?
rubric: The KB doesn't describe premium increases — whole life with premiums to age 100; exact figures are quote-screen. A pass answers from what's published (no published increase mechanism / it doesn't have that) without inventing guarantees language beyond the KB.

q: How does my client pay if she has no bank account?
rubric: Debit and credit cards are accepted alongside bank draft.

q: Whats the max day of month for drafting again - 28 or 31?
rubric: The 28th — options run 1st through 28th.

q: Payment screen: what schedule choices will I see?
rubric: Immediate draft, a chosen day of the month, a specific week-and-day of the month, or Social Security benefits billing.

q: is there a fee on top of the premium?
rubric: Yes — a $25 annual policy fee, applied according to payment frequency.

q: So on monthly mode the $25 fee adds about $2 a month?
rubric: Must not confirm the ~$2 math — the fee is $25 annually applied per frequency; exact modal amounts come from the quote screen.

q: client asks if she can prepay the whole year
rubric: Annual is one of the payment modes (monthly, quarterly, semi-annual, annual).

q: Does the payment method affect the coverage or benefits at all?
rubric: Nothing in the KB ties payment method to coverage/benefits. A pass says no such link is in its materials (the published payment facts are methods, payor, modes, draft dates, fee).

q: After issue, can she switch from monthly to annual?
rubric: The KB lists the modes but doesn't cover post-issue mode changes. A pass says it doesn't have the servicing process (human follow-up) rather than inventing one.

q: immediate draft vs future date - both possible?
rubric: Yes — payment can be an immediate draft or the first draft scheduled up to one month from the application date.

rubric: No — payor is limited to the applicant, spouse, or domestic partner; a nephew can't be the payor.

q: What account types work for the draft?
rubric: Checking or savings (ACH), and the payment screen collects the account type.

q: if the client wants to add coverage later whats the actual path
rubric: Purchase additional coverage (a separate purchase) — increases to the existing policy aren't allowed.

q: Decreases allowed all the way down to $2,000?
rubric: Yes — decreases are allowed down to the policy's minimum coverage amount ($2,000 is the product minimum).

q: Client's SS check comes the 3rd Wednesday — can drafts line up with that?
rubric: Yes — draft options include alignment with the applicant's Social Security payment date (and a specific day-within-week option).

q: whos the payor by default
rubric: The applicant (spouse or domestic partner are the other allowed options; the payment screen collects payer details when it isn't the applicant).

q: Any option to draft twice a month to split the premium?
rubric: No such option is published — modes are monthly, quarterly, semi-annually, annually. A pass gives the published modes and doesn't invent semi-monthly drafting.

q: For the first payment does she pay at application or at issue?
rubric: Payment details are collected at the payment step; the draft can be immediate or scheduled up to one month from the application date. A pass answers from those facts without inventing billing timing beyond them.

q: whats collected on the payment page besides bank numbers
rubric: The payer (applicant/spouse/domestic partner, plus payer details if not the applicant), the payment schedule, and the frequency; banking info is routing, institution, account number twice, account type.

q: can she use her husband's credit card?
rubric: Cards are an accepted method and the payor can be the spouse — with the payor's details collected when it's not the applicant. A pass connects the published payor rule (spouse allowed) to payment.

q: Draft failed and client never got a direct bill — what does the KB say should happen?
rubric: On draft failure the method defaults to direct bill; if the bill didn't arrive that's beyond the KB (human follow-up). A pass states the default-to-direct-bill rule and doesn't invent mail troubleshooting.

q: does paying annually skip the policy fee
rubric: No — the $25 annual fee applies (according to payment frequency) regardless of mode.

q: Whats the longest the client can delay the first draft?
rubric: Up to one month from the application date.

q: Client insists on a paper bill every month instead of drafting — options?
rubric: Direct bill exists in the KB only as the draft-failure default; upfront methods are draft or card. A pass presents the published methods honestly without promising monthly paper billing enrollment.

q: remind me what happens to payment method after a returned draft, and is there a retry?
rubric: The published rule: the method defaults to direct bill. No retry mechanism is published. A pass gives the direct-bill default and doesn't invent retries.
